title: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training

summary: Harness evolution from a common base exhibits Locality, Complementarity, and Nonstationarity: variants repair different failures, and their utility changes as the policy learns. Rather than seeking a universally superior harness, we introduce Harness-S to selectively rescue failures of a base execution system through sibling harnesses and transfer the resulting capabilities into a single policy that remains effective
takeaways: The same policy generates fresh rollouts under selected auxiliary harnesses, and these trajectories replace the failed group for reinforcement learning.
An Adaptive Harness Router selects the Top-k variants using Harness Behavior Profiles and voting across multiple LLMs.
Reusing the router for Rank-1 inference provides additional gains at the same executor rollout count.
